lines.text: The seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, and Passover begins at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month.
After entering the land, Israel brings the priest a sheaf of firstfruits, and he burns it before the LORD.
Israel counts fifty days and then brings two loaves of bread baked with leaven as firstfruits to the LORD.
On the first day of the seventh month, Israel has a day of rest announced by ringing bells.
The Feast of Tabernacles begins on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and runs seven days, followed by an eighth-day solemn assembly.
